question: A patient with chronic pain is not on opioids; optimized non-opioid treatment has not been effective, but the patient is not able or willing to engage in a comprehensive pain care plan. Per the VA/DoD opioid algorithm, should opioids be started?
assumption: VA/DoD opioid algorithm for chronic pain (VA guidance).
answer:
Per the VA/DoD algorithm: **No—do not start opioids in this scenario.**

For a chronic-pain patient **not currently on opioids**, after optimized non-opioid treatment is ineffective, the algorithm proceeds to opioid risk assessment and appropriate interdisciplinary/specialty consultation. If potential benefits outweigh risks, it then asks whether the patient is **able and willing to engage in a comprehensive pain care plan**. A **“No”** at that decision point leads to: **“Exit algorithm; manage with non-opioid modalities.”**

So opioids should not be initiated unless they are part of a documented comprehensive pain care plan and the patient can/will engage in it.

va_dod_cpg_opioids_2022 (VA, advisory, 2022-05)
VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Use of Opioids in the Management of Chronic Pain (Version 4.0) > Appendix J: Alternative Text Descriptions of Algorithm
[p 152]
The following outline narratively describes the Use of Opioids in the Management of Chronic Pain algorithm. An explanation of the purpose of the algorithm and description of the various shapes used within the algorithm can be found in the Algorithm section. The sidebars referenced within this outline can also be found in the Algorithm section.
A. Module A: Determination of Appropriateness for Opioids for Chronic Pain
Module A begins with Box 1, in the shape of a rounded rectangle: "Patient with chronic pain"
Box 1 connects to Box 2, in the shape of a rectangle: "Obtain pain and biopsychosocial assessment (see Sidebar A)"
Box 2 connects to Box 3, in the shape of a hexagon, and asks the question: "Is the patient currently on opioids for chronic pain?"
If the answer is "Yes" to Box 3, then continue to Box 4, in the shape of an oval: "Go to Module C"
4. If the answer is "No" to Box 3, then continue to Box 5, in the shape of a rectangle:
"Educate/re-educate on, implement, and optimize non-opioid treatments for chronic pain (see
Sidebar B), including:
Self-management to promote health and wellness
Non-opioid pharmacologic management
Non-pharmacologic pain treatments:
¨ Behavioral therapies (e.g., cognitive behavioral therapy)
¨ Physical/movement-based therapies (e.g., physical therapy)
¨ Manipulative therapies (e.g., chiropractic care)
¨ Complementary and integrative health treatments (e.g., acupuncture)
Interventional pain care (e.g., joint injection, radiofrequency ablation)
Realistic expectations and limitations of medical treatment
Refer to the LBP, OA, and Headache CPGs as appropriate for further condition-specific guidance"; VA/DoD CPGs are available here: https://www.healthquality.va.gov/
Box 5 connects to Box 6, in the shape of a hexagon, and asks the question: "After regular follow-up and treatment optimization, has the treatment plan been effective in managing pain and optimizing function?"
If the answer is "Yes" to Box 6, then continue to Box 17, in the shape of a rectangle: "Exit algorithm; manage with non-opioid modalities"
If the answer is "No" to Box 6, then continue to Box 7, in the shape of a rectangle: "Complete opioid risk assessment; refer for interdisciplinary pain and specialty consultations, as appropriate (see Sidebar C)"
[p 153]
Box 7 connects to Box 8, in the shape of a hexagon, and asks the question: "Do potential benefits outweigh risks? Consider strength and number of risk factors and patient preferences (see Sidebar C)"
If the answer is "No" to Box 8, then continue to Box 17, in the shape of a rectangle: "Exit algorithm; manage with non-opioid modalities"
If the answer is "Yes" to Box 8, then continue to Box 9, in the shape of a rectangle: "Refer/consult for appropriate interdisciplinary treatments"
Box 9 connects to Box 10, in the shape of a hexagon, and asks the question: "Is the patient able and willing to engage in a comprehensive pain care plan?"
If the answer is "No" to Box 10, then continue to Box 17, in the shape of a rectangle: "Exit algorithm; manage with non-opioid modalities"
If the answer is "Yes" to Box 10, then continue to Box 11, in the shape of a rectangle:
"Educate patient and family about treatment options, including education on:
Known risks and unknown long-term benefits of opioids
Risks of SUD and overdose
Need for risk mitigation strategies
Naloxone rescue"
Box 11 connects to Box 12, in the shape of a hexagon, and asks the question: "Is adding opioids to comprehensive pain therapy indicated at this time? (see Sidebar D)"
If the answer is "No" to Box 12, then continue to Box 17, in the shape of a rectangle: "Exit algorithm; manage with non-opioid modalities"
If the answer is "Yes" to Box 12, then Box 13, in the shape of a hexagon, asks the question: "Is patient prepared to accept responsibilities of and is provider prepared to implement risk mitigation strategies?"
If the answer is "No" to Box 13, then continue to Box 17, in the shape of a rectangle: "Exit algorithm; manage with non-opioid modalities"
If the answer is "Yes" to Box 13, then continue to Box 14, in the shape of a rectangle: "Discuss and complete written informed consent with patient and family"
Box 14 connects to Box 15, in the shape of a rectangle: "Modify and document comprehensive pain management plan including opioids"
Box 15 connects to Box 16, in the shape of an oval: "Go to Module B"
